title.description: The product title, for the listing's `listing_title`. It must READ naturally and at the same time contain the words a shopper would actually type to find this product — the product type and its one or two defining specs, in the shopper's own vocabulary. Front-load the most searched term. No keyword stuffing, no repetition, no ALL CAPS, no promotional words.

description.description: The product description, for the listing's `listing_description`. 2-4 short paragraphs of plain text (no HTML, no markdown). Say what the product is, what it is made of, how it is used, and what is included. The search terms a shopper would use must appear naturally in the prose — worked into real sentences, never listed or repeated for their own sake. Never invent specifications not supported by the data or the photos.

category.description: The product's category, for the listing's `listing_category`. Reuse a category from get_reference_values VERBATIM when one applies — it is a link to an existing Shopify Category, so a new spelling of an existing category is a broken value, and get_reference_values shows you the ones this store already uses. Only propose a different one when none of them genuinely fits, name it in the full Shopify taxonomy style, and say so in notes. Empty string if it cannot be determined.

product_type.description: The product type, for the listing's `listing_product_type` — the specific noun for what this product IS (e.g. 'Bracelet', 'Backpack', 'Fountain Pen'), not a category path. Reuse an existing product type from get_reference_values when one fits.

attributes.description: Structured product attributes as name -> value, which become the listing's Shopify metafields on publish. The named properties below are the ones nearly every listing needs; your instructions may name more, and unless they say otherwise you may ALSO add any other attribute that genuinely applies, using a lower_snake_case key and a plain-text value. Reuse an existing attribute key from get_reference_values when it means the same thing. Only include an attribute you can support from the product text or the photos. Always state the unit inside the value.

material.description: What the product is made of. Include composition percentages when given.

color.description: Colour name. When the product has colour variants, list every variant's colour comma-separated, taken from the variants you actually saw (get_product's variants and their photos), not just the prose.

size.description: Size or size range. When the product has size variants, derive the range from the actual variants. Say which scale when it is regional.

dimensions.description: Measurements, with the unit stated in the value.

weight.description: Weight, with the unit stated in the value.

images.description: Images produced by the image step, for the listing's `images` table, in the order the tool returned them — copy its result entries verbatim, including each entry's `item_variant`. An empty array when no image step ran, when the product has no photos, or when the per-request image toggle was off.

kind.description: What this image is, in the vocabulary your instructions give.

item_variant.description: The variant item code this image belongs to, copied verbatim from the image step's result entry. Null for a listing-level image — which is the value unless the image step itself set it.

source_url.description: The input photo this image was derived from, when there was one.

url.description: The resulting image, or null. Null is the normal case: the image step queues the work and it is rendered in the background after this run finishes, then attached to the listing. Copy null through as-is — it does not mean the image failed, and it does not belong in needs_review.

note.description: What the image step said about this entry, copied verbatim when it gave one. Leave null otherwise; do not write your own explanation of a null url.

variants.description: One entry per variant returned by get_product; an empty array when the product has none. This is review material for the admin — nothing in it is published automatically, and you never propose prices.

item_variant.description: The variant's item code, exactly as get_product returned it.

observed.description: Option name -> value as you actually observed it for this variant, from its photo and the product text (e.g. {"color": "Burgundy"}). Only include options you can support with evidence.

suggestions.description: Human-readable discrepancies or improvements for the admin, e.g. the catalog says 'red' but the variant photo shows burgundy. Empty when there is nothing to flag.

notes.description: Anything else the admin should know about this variant. Null when there is nothing.

needs_review.description: Human-readable names of fields that could NOT be confidently filled and must be completed by the admin before publish (e.g. 'Material', 'Product Type').

confidence.description: Overall confidence in the enrichment given the quality of the source data and photos.

notes.description: Anything the admin should know: assumptions made, ambiguities, a proposed new category, or conflicts between the product text and the photos.
